notes: Most nineteenth-century critics are cited by surname and year only, with no title (Weisse, Holtzmann, Colani, Weiffenbach, Wernle, J. Weiss, Wellhausen, Harnack, Streeter, Frankfurter, Gentry); entries carry '[Title not given.]' rather than supplied titles. Lachmann, Wilke and Weizsäcker are named only in the list of works #1746 read (l.410); Wilke and Weizsäcker have no year. Not listed as entries, too vague to cite: Eusebius (l.426, 'Irenaeus, Eusebius and the reception of EA-CORPORA-34', no work); Papias's logia (l.151, 168), Gaius, Dionysius (l.152, 158) and Origen (l.191), named as positions in the reception with no work cited; the Sinaitic Syriac (l.191, 315) and 𝔓98 and the uncials (l.239), manuscripts named as evidence; the Gospel of Thomas, 'the analogy of Thomas' (l.263, 412), named only as content of a composition; the other sources of the AI Overviews, the Bart Ehrman Blog, PBS Frontline, Catholic Answers, YouTube and Reddit (l.283), no pages named. The Septuagint books (Daniel, Ezekiel, Zechariah, Isaiah, Exodus, Gen 12:3) and the New Testament books are covered by the Swete and Nestle entries. 4 Maccabees and the Testament of Job share one snippet line. revelationfirst.com pages are the author's site, not alexanarch.org records, so they are listed. Captures (0C1D, 0C22–0C26) and EA-CORPORA seats are archive records and are left out. QAnon, Qumran sigla and Star Trek Q are named for disambiguation only.
